title: geckolib issue #891: `[1.21.1] Client crash "IllegalStateException: Not building!" when a glowing GeckoLib entity is hit (stale outline buffer reference)`
licence: GitHub issue thread: user-generated content under the GitHub Terms of Service; the repo licence (MIT) does not cover issue text
text:
[issue by SpaceOddityTr]
**Environment:** Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.248, GeckoLib 4.9.2, Mowzie's Mobs 1.8.2 (renderer in the stack, but the mechanism is GeckoLib-generic).

**Reproduction (3/3 on our pack):**
1. Summon a GeckoLib-rendered entity (observed with `mowziesmobs:umvuthi`).
2. Give it the Glowing effect (in the wild, Umvuthi's healers apply it as a game mechanic).
3. Hit the entity (melee or gunfire) while its outline is on screen.
4. Client crashes:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Not building!
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.BufferBuilder.ensureBuilding(BufferBuilder.java:76)
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.BufferBuilder.addVertex(BufferBuilder.java:156)
  at net.minecraft.client.renderer.OutlineBufferSource$EntityOutlineGenerator.addVertex(OutlineBufferSource.java:58)
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.VertexMultiConsumer$Double.addVertex(VertexMultiConsumer.java:79)  (x2)
  at software.bernie.geckolib.renderer.GeoRenderer.createVerticesOfQuad(GeoRenderer.java:341)
  at software.bernie.geckolib.renderer.GeoRenderer.renderCube(GeoRenderer.java:328)
  at com.bobmowzie.mowziesmobs.client.render.entity.MowzieGeoEntityRenderer.renderRecursively(...)
```

Notably, Glowing **alone does not crash** — we tested a glowing Umvuthana and a glowing vanilla cow standing idle. The crash requires a hit landing while the outline is rendered.

**Mechanism (verified against 1.21.1 bytecode):**

* Vanilla `OutlineBufferSource` backs all glow outlines with **one shared immediate `BufferSource`**; requesting a different `RenderType` from an immediate source **ends the previous builder**.
* `GeoRenderer` fetches the (outline-wrapping) `VertexConsumer` once and holds it across the whole bone pass.
* When the hit lands, something re-enters the same outline source with another render type mid-pass (hurt overlay / held item / a render layer — the exact trigger doesn't change the picture). The shared builder is ended; GeckoLib keeps writing through the stale `EntityOutlineGenerator` reference; the next `addVertex` throws.

**Suggested fix:** re-fetch the buffer from the `MultiBufferSource` whenever the render type can have changed within the bone pass (or per bone/cube batch), instead of holding one `VertexConsumer` across code that may switch render types. Alternatively, catching the ended-builder state before writing would make the outline path tolerant.

**Our modpack-local workaround** (shipped, works): a small client mixin on `EntityOutlineGenerator` that skips writes when the delegate `BufferBuilder` is no longer building — the outline loses one frame instead of crashing the client.

This looks related to older reports of "Not building!" with GeckoLib entities in villages (e.g. irons-spells-n-spellbooks#536, closed as not-their-bug) — same signature, so the root may affect multiple GeckoLib consumers.

Prior art in this tracker: #606 "[1.21] Buffer Builder Not Building! with glowing item/armor render layers on 4.5.7" (closed Aug 2024, "fixed once more in 4.6"). That fix co
[... truncated]

[comment by Tslat (collaborator)]
Yeah GeckoLib already does this:

https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/0d9d3ea311c93f99276b596eee9b5f69d2e0db92/common/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib/renderer/GeoRenderer.java#L266

The problem is it can't account for custom buffer types.

This bug happens when someone attempts  to render something out of order (such as rendering a glow layer right in the middle of rendering its normal layer).

In this case it looks like mowzies itself is bypassing Geckolib's normal render cycle, which means any patch I do on my side is useless

This really needs to be fixed on the mowzies side, I don't think there's a lot more I can do on my side
